content.title: About
content.content: The Whole Grain Muffin (2598) is a baked product made from whole grain flour, a small amount of sugar, and vegetable oil. It has a soft, slightly moist crumb and a gentle nutty aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain muffins retain most of the fiber and micronutrients of the grain.
The recipe often includes rolled oats, whole wheat, and whole rye.
Because whole grains are used, these muffins have a lower glycemic index than typical white muffins.
Traditionally they are served at breakfast with yogurt, fruit, or honey.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Whole grains provide both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting digestive health.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Complex carbs deliver sustained energy and promote satiety.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2 and B3 aid carbohydrate metabolism and support the nervous system.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: The muffin supplies magnesium, iron and zinc, important for muscle and immune function.

items.title: Low in trans fats
items.content: When prepared with non‑hydrogenated vegetable oil, trans‑fat content remains minimal.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Contains wheat, so it is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although modest, the sugar should be accounted for by those monitoring blood glucose.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Whole grain muffins still provide calories, so portion control is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the muffin as a snack, split it and spread cottage cheese, nut butter, or avocado. It pairs well with berries, honey, or low‑fat yogurt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store muffins in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer keeping, refrigerate up to 7 days or freeze in a zip‑lock bag.
